title: Alberta Home EV Charger Rebate 2026: What Is Open
desc: There is no open home EV charger rebate for Alberta houses in 2026. ChargeYYC and ZEVIP are closed. Here is what a home charger costs and what does exist.
h1: Alberta Home EV Charger Rebates in 2026
badge: No open home charger rebate found
lead: If you own a house in Alberta and want a charger in your garage, we could not find any rebate you can apply for today. We checked the federal, city and utility programs. Here is what we found, what closed, and how to keep the cost down anyway.
cards_heading: What we checked for Alberta home chargers
cards_intro: Each card names the official page we read on October 3, 2026.

cards.title: Calgary ChargeYYC
cards.note: For buildings with 3 or more units on a shared electrical service: up to $6,000 per stall for wiring and up to $1,000 or $2,000 per charger. Phase 2 applications closed November 18, 2025. Detached houses were never eligible.

cards.title: Federal ZEVIP
cards.note: Natural Resources Canada funds chargers in public places, workplaces, fleets and multi-unit buildings, at 50% of costs. It does not fund individual homeowners, and the owner and operator streams are closed for applications.

cards.title: Federal EV Affordability Program
cards.note: Open from February 16, 2026 until March 31, 2031 or until funds run out. It helps you buy or lease an eligible electric vehicle. It does not pay for a home charger.

cards.title: Federal iZEV
cards.note: The old federal EV incentive paid up to $5,000 toward a vehicle. It ended March 31, 2025.

cards.title: ENMAX
cards.note: ENMAX's EV charger guide gives advice but lists no home charger rebate. It says Level 2 chargers start at $499 before installation.

after_cards: We have not confirmed every Alberta utility or town. If your bill comes from EPCOR, ATCO, FortisAlberta or a local co-op, ask them directly. If any of them start a program, we will add it here.
sections: ENMAX says a Level 2 charger starts at $499, before installation. The bigger cost is often the wiring, and sometimes the electrical panel. A full charge takes about 6 to 14 hours for a battery electric car on Level 2, so most people charge overnight.
How to avoid a panel upgrade

A panel upgrade can cost more than the charger. ENMAX suggests two ways around it. First, a smaller charger, such as 30 amps instead of 50, is often enough: ENMAX says the average driver needs under 3 hours of charging a night. Second, an EV energy management system can share power between the charger and the rest of your home. ENMAX puts that at about $1,200. Ask your electrician for a load calculation before you decide.
Permits and who can do the work

In Calgary, new wiring for an EV charger needs an electrical permit. A homeowner permit costs $116.50, but the City says homeowners cannot install EV charging wiring themselves, change the main service or do the load calculation. A licensed electrician must do that. Condo owners need a licensed contractor, and row-house units need condo board approval and a load calculation. Other cities have their own permit rules, so check with yours.
Living in a condo or apartment?

Most of the money that did exist went to multi-unit buildings, not houses. Calgary's ChargeYYC and the federal ZEVIP both funded chargers for shared parking, and both are closed for now. If your building is planning chargers, ask your board to watch for the next round.
claim_heading: How to add a home charger in Alberta
claim_steps: Hire a licensed electrician and ask for a load calculation first.
Choose a charger size that fits your panel; 30 amps is often enough.
If your panel is short, compare an energy management system with a panel upgrade.
Make sure the electrician pulls the electrical permit.
Ask your utility if a charger rebate has opened since we checked.
faq: Is there a home EV charger rebate in Alberta?
We found none open for houses in 2026. Calgary's ChargeYYC was only for multi-unit buildings and closed in November 2025, and federal ZEVIP does not fund individual homeowners.
Does the federal EV program pay for a home charger?
No. The Electric Vehicle Affordability Program helps with buying or leasing an eligible vehicle, not the charger.
How much does a Level 2 charger cost in Alberta?
ENMAX says chargers start at $499 before installation. Wiring, permits and any panel work add to that.
Can I install the wiring myself in Calgary?
No. The City of Calgary says homeowners cannot install EV charging wiring; a licensed electrician must, with a permit.
Do I need a 50 amp charger?
Often not. ENMAX says the average driver needs under 3 hours of charging a night, so a 30 amp charger may be enough and can avoid a panel upgrade.
